message.reasoning:
Let me assess each criterion.

C1: Mission concept and rationale (40% weight → max 40, levels map 7-10 → likely scaled: level marks 7-10 out of 10 then ×4? The rubric says max 40 with levels 7-10 etc. So mark within level range then scaled by weight? Simplest: choose level descriptor and whole-number mark within level's range. But max is 40. Hmm. Ambiguity: the levels' min/max are 7-10, 4-6, 0-3, which is out of 10. With weight 40, the mark should probably be level mark × 4. I'll report mark on the 0-40 scale: e.g. 9/10 → 36. Let me compute.

C1: Clear mission, goal, objectives (4 numbered), users (AIMS operator, GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM), rationale with references. Strong. Slight issues: objective 2 "10 m GSD" from a Nature news article; bathymetry mention 100 m resolution. Overall Accomplished, mark 9 → 36/40.

C2: Project plan (30): Gantt chart present (Figure 1), task descriptions, contingencies, risks table, information sources table, software (STK via lab licence), links plan to mission. Very good. Minor: Gantt chart dates columns labeled oddly (Wk2 21/9, Wk 4 5/10, Wk 5 12/10 — should be 12/10? Actually weekly: 21/9, 28/9, 5/10, 12/10, 19/10, 26/10, 2/11, 9/11, 16/11 — header shows "Wk 4 5/10, Wk 5 12/10" yes correct... header shows Wk2 21/9, Wk3 28/9, Wk4 5/10, Wk5 12/10, Wk6 19/10, Wk7 26/10, Wk8 2/11, Wk9 9/11, Wk10 16/11. That's consistent, 9 columns. Fine.

One issue: "Launch Specifics" band, "Orbit Specifics" etc. Good. Accomplished, 9 → 27/30.

C3: Preliminary progress (10%): Background reading, STK tutorials, hand calcs table with period, orbits/day, inclination, ground track shift, swath, interpretation. Good. Check numbers: a=6978, T=2π√(a³/μ). a³ = 6978³ = 3.398e11 km³. /398600 = 8.524e5 s². sqrt = 923.3 s. ×2π = 5801 s ✓. Orbits/day 14.9 ✓. Inclination for 600 km SSO ~97.8° ✓ (typical ~97.8-98°). Ground track shift: 360×5801/86164 = 24.24° → at equator 24.24° × 111.32 = 2699 km ✓. Swath: 6000 px × 10 m = 60 km ✓. Reef width 250 km — actually the GBR is up to ~250 km wide in the south, ok. Interpretation reasonable.

But a discrepancy: ground track spacing 2700 km per orbit means adjacent tracks on the same day are far apart; weekly coverage with a 60 km swath and 14.9 orbits/day gives... Actually total orbit tracks per week ~104, equatorial spacing ~ 360/14.9 = 24° each day but successive days shift; over a week, tracks fill in ~ 104 tracks spread over 360° of longitude but latitude range limited. Hmm, the argument is roughly right that weekly full coverage at 60 km swath is not guaranteed. Fine. However inclination 97.8° gives near-polar orbit; at 250 km width reef, and track spacing near equator 2700 km within a day, but after a week ~104 orbits spaced 24.2° apart... So the claim is defensible.

Accomplished: 8 → 8/10.

C4: Presentation (20): Well written, clear structure, figures/tables labelled, references cited in text matching list. Check citations: [1]-[11] all appear? [1] yes, [2] yes, [3] yes, [4] yes, [5] yes, [6] yes, [7] yes (Table 2), [8] yes, [9] yes, [10] yes, [11] yes. Reference list has all. Good. Minor issues: reference [4] is a Nature news article used for a technical requirement (weak but ok). Gantt chart says gold=complete, blue=planned — the chart shows Background Research Wk2-3 gold, Strategies Wk3 gold; ok. Reference formatting generally consistent IEEE. Accomplished 9 → 18/20.

Total ~ 36+27+8+18 = 89.

Requirements:
R1 met. R2 met (plan relates to space segment: launch, orbit, ground control, comms, EOL; though preliminary hand calcs cover orbit). R3 met (STK, mentions PIGI fallback and registering for licence). R4 met. R5 met. R6 met.

Technical issues:
- Reference [4] is a news article supporting 10 m GSD requirement — weak justification; the Nature news piece is about airborne (CAO) mapping, not satellite; the 10 m GSD "to be refined against the method in [4]" is hand-wavy.
- Objective claim "current satellites have only mapped GBR depths to resolution of 100 m per pixel" citation [3] — that's a depth model (gbr100), not satellite-derived; minor mischaracterisation.
- Sun-synchronous inclination 97.8° at 600 km: fine (~97.79°).
- "nodal precession of 0.9856° per day" correct.
- 60 km swath at 600 km altitude with 6000 pixels implies IFOV ~10 µrad... 60 km/600 km = 0.1 rad = 5.7°, pixel 6000 across → 1e-5 rad = 10 µrad, diffraction aperture ~ λ/θ = 0.5µm/1e-5 = 5 cm — plausible, not addressed.
- Ground track shift uses 86,164 s sidereal day, appropriate.
- Weekly coverage analysis: 60 km swath, and statement "reef up to 250 km wide ... five neighbouring passes" — but neighbouring passes in a single day are 2700 km apart, so neighbouring passes at the equator are days apart; over a week only ~7 tracks near a given latitude — so 5 passes covering 250 km width would take ~5 weeks not 1 week. The interpretation slightly understates the problem but correctly flags infeasibility. Could note.
- Reference [11] lacks author.
- Objective 1 "image full length of reef 2,300 km once a week" — with 60 km swath and polar orbit, full-length along-track coverage feasible per pass, but cross-track coverage issue. Fine.
- Figure 1 date column "Wk 2 21/9" — 21 Sep 2020 was Monday; ok.

Also possible issue: sun-synchronous orbit at fixed local time gives consistent illumination but the mission says daylight imaging; not explicitly discussed—minor.

Level marks: C1 36/40, C2 27/30, C3 8/10, C4 18/20. Total 89.
